urn:eigenius:core:description: The OBO Foundry — the collaborative of biomedical-ontology developers that maintains the shared principles and the OBO term namespace, and the declarer of the OBO meta-vocabulary below. Minted by the D72 migration: `declared_by` is resource-typed, so the value these terms already carried needed a resource to name.

OBO synonym with scope `exact` — the value is interchangeable with the term's canonical label (e.g. `cell nucleus` for the GO class `nucleus`). Populated by the obograph importer from `meta.synonyms[*]` entries whose `pred` slot is `hasExactSynonym`. Multi-valued: a Resource may carry many exact synonyms. Indexed for text retrieval alongside `core:description` so `~` queries find Resources by any of their declared names.

OBO synonym with scope `related` — the value is associated with the term but neither a strict exact alias nor narrower/broader (e.g. a colloquial name with imprecise mapping). Populated from `meta.synonyms[*]` entries whose `pred` is `hasRelatedSynonym`.

OBO synonym with scope `broad` — the value names a category strictly more general than the term. Populated from `meta.synonyms[*]` entries whose `pred` is `hasBroadSynonym`. Useful for retrieval queries that want to surface broader-context matches alongside exact ones.
OBO synonym with scope `narrow` — the value names a more specific subtype or subclass of the term. Populated from `meta.synonyms[*]` entries whose `pred` is `hasNarrowSynonym`.

OBO RBox axiom — asserts that the subject Property is the inverse of the object Property under OWL semantics (`P inverseOf Q` ⇔ `?x P ?y` iff `?y Q ?x`). The obograph importer maps the OBO bare-string `inverseOf` edge predicate to this Property. Eigenius does not currently derive the inverse triples automatically; the slot is recorded for downstream consumers that want to honour the axiom.
